title: C482/1167/2023 of RAJEEV REKHI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
05.06.2024 C482 No. 4 of 2024
With
C482 No. 1167 of 2023
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for
the applicant, Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief
Holder for the State and Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary,
learned counsel for the respondent.
2. On 06.03.2024, the applicant Amit
Rekhi was present through V.C and respondent
No. 2 Arzoo was also present with her father;
however, on that day, initially this Court observed
that there are possibilities of amicable settlement
in between the parties but come to the
conclusion that there are possibilities that
applicant and respondent No. 2 will live together
for which they want some more time for
discussion with elder members of the family.
3. Thereafter, the matter was listed
before this Court on 26.04.2024 and this Court
interacted with the parties and on that day, Mrs.
Meenakshi Sharma, learned counsel was also
appointed as mediator to mediate in between the
parties and after post-lunch sessions, the parties
come up with the settlement that a sum of Rs.

80.00 lakh will be paid by the applicant to the
respondent within a month towards full and final
settlement. It was also agreed in between the
parties that all the pending proceedings either
criminal or civil, they will move a proper
application for withdrawal of all those
proceedings. They further agreed that they will
get divorce by way of mutual consent by moving
an application under Section 13-B of the Hindu
Marriage Act. Consequently, this Court directed
both the parties to file an affidavit within four
weeks.
4. Today, the matter is again listed
before this Court; however, no affidavit has been
filed in compliance to the earlier order dated
26.04.2024. Today, the father of the applicant
and father of the respondent No. 2 are also
present in Court.
5. Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel who
appears for the applicant submits that he is
having three bank drafts of Rs. 80.00 lakh. He has
handed over the same to the father of the
respondent today in the Court, the photocopy of
the same is also placed before this Court and the
same is taken on record.
6. It is submitted by the learned counsel

for the parties that the applicant is in abroad and
it is very difficult for him to pursue the divorce
petition, for which a settlement has been arrived
that they will move an application under Section
13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act. Mr. Jitendra
Chaudhary, learned counsel for the respondent
No. 2 informs to this Court that respondent No. 2
has already filed a divorce petition under Section
13(i)(a) of the Hindu Marriage Act in the Court of
Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun and he
submits that since the applicant is not in a
position to come to the country, therefore, the
said divorce petition be treated as a divorce
petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu
Marriage Act.
7. The Court of Principal Judge, Family
Court, Dehradun is directed to convert the
divorce petition filed under Section 13(i)(a) of
Hindu Marriage Act to a petition under Section
13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act and the same be
expedited as early as possible as per law and the
applicant is directed to appear through his father,
being holder of special power of attorney of the
applicant.
8. Since now the parties have settled
their dispute and amount of Rs. 80.00 lakh

towards permanent alimony has been given to
the father of the respondent through bank draft
in the Court, who is present in Court and he
admits that he has received the bank draft of Rs.
80.00 lakh. Accordingly, the present C482
Applications are disposed of finally with direction
to the Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun to
expedite the divorce petition by converting it to
the divorce petition under Section 13-B of the
Hindu Marriage Act. The Principal Judge, Family
Court, Dehradun is also directed to give a
particular date so that the parties may present
before it for expeditious disposal of the divorce
petition and as stated in the preceding paragraph,
the Principal Judge, Family Court permit the
applicant to appear through his father being a
special power of attorney holder.
9. Since now the parties have settled
their dispute, there is no useful purpose to
continue with the pending proceedings, which are
the subject matter of the present C482
Applications.
10. Accordingly, the proceedings of
Criminal Case 2172 of 2023, State Vs. Amit Rekhi
and others pending in the Court of Additional
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun, challenged in

C-482 Application No. 4 of 2024 and the
proceeding of Criminal Case No. 7433 of 2023,
pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Dehradun, challenged in C482 Application No.
1167 of 2023 are hereby quashed.
11. Both the C482 Applications stand
disposed of.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 05.06.2024
Mahinder/
